title: Phineus and the Harpies

scope.description: The Argonauts find Phineus tormented by Harpies, and Boreas' sons drive them away.
scope.boundaryRationale: One paragraph gives Phineus' affliction and the Harpies' pursuit before the Symplegades unit.

evidence.sourceText: Having repeated this tale to his companions, the two sons of Boreas, who were also in the Argo, begged permission to drive them away.

On another occasion, when Jason visited Phineus, the blind king of Thrace, he heard that this monarch's life was imbittered by the Harpies, vile monsters, part woman, part bird, who ate or befouled all the food placed before him, and never let him eat a mouthful in peace.
